trial_name.text: VICTORIA (VerICiguaT GlObal Study in Subjects With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection FrAction)

citations.quote: VICTORIA VerICiguaT GIObal Study in Subjects With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection FrAction
VICTORIA VerICiguaT GIObal Study in Subjects With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection FrAction
The primary evidence of effectiveness is from one Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, event-driven, multicenter clinical trial (VICTORIA)

design.text: Randomized, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, double-blind, event-driven, multi-center trial comparing vericiguat (up to 10 mg daily, started at 2.5 mg once daily and doubled every 2 weeks to the target maintenance dose) to matching placebo on a background of standard of care HF therapies; subjects randomized 1:1.

citations.quote: VICTORIA was a randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multi-center, double-blind, event-driven trial comparing vericiguat to placebo in subjects with HFrEF.

Eligible subjects were randomized to vericiguat up to 10 mg daily or matching placebo in a 1:1 ratio and stratified according to geographical region and race. Study medication was to be taken in addition to regional standard of care HF therapies.
Dosing regimen	Start 2.5 mg once daily (taken with food) and double the dose every 2 weeks to reach the target maintenance dose of 10 mg once daily

population.text: Adults ≥18 years with chronic HF (NYHA Class II-IV) and reduced ejection fraction (LVEF < 45%), elevated natriuretic peptides, and a previous HF decompensation (defined as HF hospitalization within 6 months before randomization or use of IV diuretics for HF within 3 months before randomization).

citations.quote: The trial enrolled adults \ge 18 years of age with chronic HF (NYHA Class II-IV) with reduced ejection fraction (< 45%), elevated levels of natriuretic peptides, and previous HF decompensation (defined as HF hospitalization within 6 months before randomization or use of IV diuretics for HF within 3 months before randomization).

endpoint.text: Time to the first occurrence of the composite of CV death or HF hospitalization.

citations.quote: Time to the first occurrence of the composite of CV death or HF hospitalization.

result.text: Primary composite endpoint (CV death or HF hospitalization) occurred in 897 (35.5%) vericiguat vs 972 (38.5%) placebo; HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.82, 0.98); p=0.019, with a 4.2% annualized absolute risk reduction.

citations.quote: Over the course of the study, there was a 4.2% annualized absolute risk reduction (ARR) with VERQUVO compared with placebo.

indication.text: Indicated to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and heart failure (HF) hospitalization following a hospitalization for heart failure or need for outpatient IV diuretics, in adults with symptomatic chronic HF and ejection fraction less than 45%.

citations.quote: VERQUVO™ is indicated to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and heart failure (HF) hospitalization following a hospitalization for heart failure or need for outpatient IV diuretics, in adults with symptomatic chronic HF and ejection fraction less than 45% [see *Clinical Studies* (14)].

target_moa.text: Vericiguat is a stimulator of soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), an enzyme in the nitric oxide (NO) signaling pathway; sGC stimulation increases intracellular cGMP, a signaling molecule involved in vascular smooth muscle relaxation, cardiac contractility, and cardiac remodeling.

citations.quote: Vericiguat is a stimulator of soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), an important enzyme in the nitric oxide (NO) signaling pathway.
Soluble guanylate cyclase stimulates production of cGMP, a signaling molecule involved in vascular smooth muscle relaxation, cardiac contractility, and cardiac remodeling.

modality.text: Small molecule (oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator)

citations.quote: Pharmacologic class	SGC stimulator
Dosage Form and Strength	2.5 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg film-coated tablets

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were hypotension (16% vericiguat vs 15% placebo) and anemia (10% vs 7%). Principal adverse drug reactions of interest were symptomatic hypotension, syncope, and anemia (each ~4% annual likelihood).

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions reported in ≥5% are hypotension and anemia. (6.1)

Hypotension	16	15
Anemia	10	7
The annual likelihood of experiencing one of the principal adverse drug reactions (symptomatic hypotension, syncope, and anemia) are in a similar range as the efficacy—approximately 4%.

detail.text: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — Do not administer VERQUVO to a pregnant female because it may cause fetal harm; exclude pregnancy before treatment and use effective contraception during treatment and for one month after stopping.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY

**Females of reproductive potential:** Exclude pregnancy before the start of treatment. To prevent pregnancy, females of reproductive potential must use effective forms of contraception during treatment and for one month after stopping treatment. Do not administer VERQUVO to a pregnant female because it may cause fetal harm [see *Dosage and Administration* (2.2), *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1), and *Use in Specific Populations* (8.3)].

detail.text: The Division of Risk Management and the Division of Cardiology and Nephrology determined that a REMS is not needed to ensure the benefits of vericiguat outweigh its risks; the risk of embryo-fetal toxicity is communicated through labeling.

citations.quote: Division of Risk Management (DRM) and the Division of Cardiology and Nephrology (DCN) determined that a REMS is not needed to ensure the benefits of vericiguat outweigh its risks.

vote.text: An advisory committee meeting was not convened; the study design, endpoints, and statistical plan were typical and results clear and non-controversial.

citations.quote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened to discuss this application. The study design, endpoints, and statistical plan were typical of studies for this indication, and the results were clear and non-controversial. No safety issues were identified that might have benefitted from a public discussion.

summary.text: Vericiguat received fast track designation in 2014 under IND 116743 for HFrEF; the NDA (submitted May 2020) was granted priority review status on July 14, 2020 and was approved first-cycle without an advisory committee based on the single Phase 3 VICTORIA trial.

citations.quote: Vericiguat received fast track designation in 2014 under its IND 116743 for the treatment of HFrEF and this NDA application received priority review status on July 14, 2020.
The NDA was submitted in May 2020 and was granted priority review status.
The primary evidence of effectiveness is from one Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, event-driven, multicenter clinical trial (VICTORIA)
An advisory committee meeting was not convened to discuss this application.
